clue.text: Poor ref in action? It's too much

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside another, here the shuffled referee letters inside the lawsuit

parts.note: an action at law is a lawsuit, a suit

indicators.note: poor suggests something done badly, so the letters of ref are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football fan complains that a bad referee's performance has been more than anyone could bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' is not a deed here but a case brought in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess, more of something than is wanted.

clue.text: Boss keeps fellows needing 17 energy well fed

indicators.note: keeps means the boss holds the next pieces inside it, a container signal

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob on a surface
F is the abbreviation for fellow, doubled for the plural
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An employer retains staff who need more get-up-and-go, and everyone is well fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' here is the ornamental knob on a shield or ceiling, not an employer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stuffed has eaten their fill, a synonym for well fed.

clue.text: Polished vertical surface in part of a musical instrument

indicators.note: in places the vertical surface inside the instrument part, a container signal

parts.note: a reed is the vibrating part of a clarinet or oboe mouthpiece
an aircraft's fin is the vertical surface on its tail

explanation.surface: A polished upright panel set into a piece of an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined manners or metal are cultivated or smoothed, a synonym of polished.

clue.text: Show feeling over English 21 book that's turned up

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the reversed book sits above the letter for English
in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top, so the book word runs backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone gets emotional over an English book that has been found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's turned up' reverses TOME to EMOT, and 'over' stacks it above E in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to display emotion theatrically.

clue.text: Grab what's given out and 23 make an argument of it

parts.note: to grab is to take
an issue is something given out, like a magazine issue or supplies issued

explanation.surface: Someone seizes a handout and starts a quarrel over it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take issue is to dispute or disagree, raising an argument.

clue.text: Understand about changing last conceptual pattern

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the understand word goes round the rest

parts.note: to get something is to understand it

indicators.note: changing indicates that the letters of last are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thinker grasps that reordering the final item alters the overall design.
explanation.definitionFit: A gestalt is an organised whole perceived as more than its parts, a pattern of perception.

clue.text: Signal for dinner catches one on the point of 24 departure

indicators.note: catches means the gong holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a gong is struck to call people to dinner
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The dinner gong rings just as a guest is about to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Going can mean about to leave, as in 'are you going now?'

clue.text: Belt of tan colour inside and identical outside

indicators.note: inside, together with outside, says the colour sits within the word for identical

parts.note: identical means the same
tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: A tan belt that matches both inside and out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' and 'outside' work together as one container signal. Sam Browne is a military belt with a shoulder strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sam Browne is an officer's leather belt with a strap over the shoulder.

clue.text: Polluted area to right — one injects gas

indicators.note: polluted means spoiled or mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dirty patch to the right of a man pumping gas.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerator is a device forcing air into a liquid or soil.

clue.text: Best possible spot to follow article

indicators.note: to follow puts the rearranged spot after the article

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: possible here means one possible arrangement of the letters of spot

explanation.surface: Choosing the best possible place to come after a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best possible' looks like one phrase, but 'possible' is the anagram signal: SPOT becomes TOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The tops is a colloquial superlative for the very best.

clue.text: Remove priest having undue fun with music

indicators.note: undue suggests improper or out of place, so the letters of fun are rearranged

parts.note: rock is a kind of music

explanation.surface: A clergyman is defrocked for having too much fun with rock music.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfrock is to strip a clergyman of his office.

clue.text: Dip? I am seen by English river mostly

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: mostly means the river's name loses its last letter

parts.note: the Mersey is the river through Liverpool

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quick swim in an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: To immerse something is to plunge it in liquid, to dip it.

clue.text: Noted string technique in pilfering

explanation.surface: A thief's fingers are as nimble on a violin as in a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingering is how a player places fingers on strings, and also slang for stealing, to finger being to pilfer.

clue.text: Something from the past gets one a kind of rocket

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned item comes with a rocket of a sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro is old-style fashion, and a retro is also a braking rocket fired against the direction of motion.

clue.text: In 24 hours theologian will be a father

indicators.note: In puts the theologian inside the day, a container signal

parts.note: twenty-four hours make a day
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: Within a day a scholar of divinity becomes a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Daddy is a familiar word for one's father.

clue.text: Sea is hot, as is the sun

parts.note: the Yellow Sea lies between China and Korea
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A sunny day: the sea is warm, and so is the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea' gives only YELLOW, the first word of the Yellow Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun is usually pictured as a pale golden colour, tinged with yellow.

clue.text: Parts of hospital not looking ahead?

explanation.surface: Rooms at the hospital that face sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: Side wards are small rooms off a main ward, and sidewards means towards the side, not forwards.

clue.text: Maybe deceive about time twice? He should see through it

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters given may be arranged another way
twice means the time letter is used two times

explanation.surface: Someone might try to fool the clock twice over, but an investigator will spot it.
explanation.walkthrough: DECEIVE with two Ts, all mixed by 'Maybe', gives a sleuth; 'about' only joins, meaning 'with regard to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective's job is to uncover deceit, seeing through a ruse.

clue.text: Lament nun sadly getting legal cancellation

indicators.note: sadly here signals the letters of lament and nun are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun grieves over a court ruling that voids something.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulment is a legal declaration that a marriage or act is void.

clue.text: Prayer of theatrical backer to us

parts.note: an angel is an investor who finances a stage show

explanation.surface: A prayer from a financier of a show directed to us.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is a Catholic devotion said at morning, noon and evening.

clue.text: No talking bird has Latin, not really

parts.note: a mina or myna is a bird that mimics speech

explanation.surface: A parrot that cannot speak Latin, though in name only.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominal means in name only, existing as a token rather than in fact.

clue.text: Throw out of multiplex pell-mell

indicators.note: of says the answer is taken out of the words that follow, which run across the word break

explanation.surface: Ejected from the multiplex cinema in a mad rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to eject or drive someone out.

clue.text: Trim ape, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of trim ape are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to groom a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an ape is one kind of primate.
explanation.definitionFit: Apes belong to the order of mammals that also includes monkeys and humans.

clue.text: Support to a diminished extent, being drunk

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
less means to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: Propped up a bit less, being tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless is British slang for very drunk, unable to stand.

clue.text: Old boy with beaker brought back okra pods

indicators.note: brought back means the joined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a mug is a drinking vessel, a beaker

explanation.surface: A former pupil brings a cup back containing okra.
explanation.walkthrough: OB plus MUG gives OBMUG, which 'brought back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumbo is a name for okra, and for the stew thickened with it.

clue.text: Power playwright shows in expression of dismissal

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A powerful dramatist shows his disdain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pshaw is an interjection voicing contempt or impatience.

clue.text: In front of a leading teacher

parts.note: the head is the head teacher, who leads a school

explanation.surface: A head teacher stands before the class.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead means in front or in the lead.

clue.text: Rather extensive pine is 6 hard

parts.note: to pine is to long for something
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fairly long pine tree is tough timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' is the verb to long for, not the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Longish means somewhat long, rather extended in length.

clue.text: Repeat it, not quietly, 7 perhaps? Perhaps

definitions.text: Repeat it, not quietly, 7 perhaps? Perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the remaining letters may be arranged another way
not signals that the following quiet letter is taken out of the words before

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quietly

explanation.surface: A performer is told to say something again, but louder this time.
explanation.walkthrough: REPEAT IT without its P gives REEATIT, which 'perhaps' rearranges; the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do again, to repeat.

clue.text: Sarah has food, an 8 ice-skater's speciality

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the name Sarah
chow is slang for food

explanation.surface: Sarah eats a meal before her skating routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A Salchow is a figure-skating jump named after Ulrich Salchow.

clue.text: Some attend lessons out of 14 term?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pupil goes to some classes outside school time.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'not within the school term', but means having no term or limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless means having no end, without a limit or term.
